name: Mesh Finisher
author: Modly fork (Finish ported from image-to-3dlab by Bingeljell, Apache-2.0)
description: Turn a generated high-poly asset into a game-ready one: retopologise (voxel remesh + decimate), transfer the texture, re-project the source photo's real pixels (Pixel Match), bake normal + metallic-roughness detail from the original, then compress textures. Needs Blender 4.2 or newer for the retopology and bake stages.

params_schema.label: Target Face Count
params_schema.tooltip: Low-poly target the retopologised mesh lands on (decimation is measured against triangles, so the result is close to this). Too few loses the silhouette; too many re-fragments the texture atlas.

params_schema.label: Voxel Size (fraction)
params_schema.tooltip: Voxel remesh cell size as a fraction of the asset's largest side. Rebuilds one watertight surface before decimation — decimating the raw generated mesh shatters thin geometry. 0 skips the remesh.

params_schema.label: Atlas Size
params_schema.tooltip: Size of the texture atlas the original texture is transferred onto.

params_schema.label: Pixel Match

options.label: Auto (when a Source Photo is connected)

params_schema.tooltip: Keeps the source photo's real pixels: fits a camera to the mesh and paints every surface it can see, so text, logos and faces come through exactly instead of as a redrawn lookalike.

params_schema.label: Bake Surface Detail
params_schema.tooltip: Bake a normal map (and the original's metallic-roughness map) from the high-poly onto the finish, so it lights like the dense original.

params_schema.label: Compress Textures
params_schema.tooltip: Re-encode embedded textures (colour capped at the atlas size, maps at 1024, JPEG quality 90). Large size drop; stays core glTF so every converter reads it.

params_schema.label: Metallic (fallback)
params_schema.tooltip: Flat metallic factor used while the bake is off or when no metallic-roughness map could be transferred.

params_schema.label: Roughness (fallback)
params_schema.tooltip: Flat roughness factor used while the bake is off or when no metallic-roughness map could be transferred.
